root_idea.summary: A root centered on putting something or someone at a distance, driving it away, or causing separation.
root_idea.development: From physical removal, the lexicon extends to pursuing or hunting, attacking, successive following, and orderly or continuous progression by comparison with one thing driving or following another.

senses.definition: To drive away, expel, or remove someone from one's presence or place, treating the person as unwanted or contemptible.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I verb; in the Quran it concerns sending people away or refusing to retain them among one's company.

senses.definition: One who drives away or expels.
senses.usage_conditions: Active participle of طَرَدَ; in the Quran it is used of a person who would drive believers away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive, bring, or gather camels together from their separate quarters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I use specifically attested with camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pursue, course, hunt, trap, or catch wild animals and similar game.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A hunting use of Form I; طَرَدٌ and طِرَادٌ can denote the activity of pursuing game.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come upon a people, pass through them, or destroy them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form I usage reported with a people or group as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the wind, to blow pebbles and dust away with violence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended use in which the wind performs the driving-away action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a plain to have the mirage run along it like water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression applied to plains and mirage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To direct one's observation or attention to an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form I construction with the eye or observation as the thing directed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put forward opposition or contradiction in a question.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression used of disputation or disagreement in an issue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prolong or extend the voice; also, to extend or stretch out a whip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II extended usage; the vocal and whip constructions are reported together under this derived form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a judge to tell a litigant to invalidate or challenge the testimony of witnesses, if able.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative Form II construction in judicial procedure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To charge upon, assault, attack, and fight an adversary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal combat sense of Form III; the opponents may each charge the other whether either drives the other away or not.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a horse run in a race.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended Form III use associated with racing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause or order someone to be driven away, expelled, banished, or placed at a distance, especially from a town or country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use; it may describe an authority ordering expulsion or banishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To order that camels be driven, brought, or gathered together from their separate quarters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative construction with camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send the he-goats among a herd.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV livestock usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For one about to race another, to propose a wager tied to who outstrips whom.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV racing construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For two opponents to charge upon, assault, and fight each other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI combat use, whether or not either opponent drives the other away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To proceed in an uninterrupted, orderly, or consistent sequence; hence for water, affairs, speech, recitation, definitions, rules, or usage to follow a regular course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended Form VIII sense of one part following another; with rules and usage it denotes regular or consistently applicable conformity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To desire or seek to drive away, expel, banish, or place at a distance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X desiderative or seeking use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To retreat or wheel widely from an adversary in battle as a stratagem, then return upon him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized combat construction in which the withdrawal draws an opponent from an untenable position to one that can be attacked.

other_classical_meanings.definition: By way of digression, with something mentioned outside its proper place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun-based expression derived from the stratagem of drawing away and returning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Possibly a sucker or offset of a palm tree, as though pushed forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted entry is explicitly uncertain and may contain a textual error.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water in which animals have waded and voided urine and dung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of water rendered impure or fouled by animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A charge or assault in which two horsemen attack each other at the same time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a simultaneous paired cavalry charge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular food associated with the Kurds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical item with no broader semantic restriction supplied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A straight, direct, or even course of walking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended noun use describing the manner of walking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or animal driven away, expelled, banished, or outcast; also a removed or distant one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective may be applied to a female as well as a male, and can describe a she-camel without a feminine ending.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One born after another; by extension, either of two successive entities such as night and day.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry also reports an opposing usage for one born before another; the central image is succession as if one follows or drives another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Old or worn-out, applied to a garment or piece of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended adjectival use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The base or lower part of a palm-tree raceme.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical noun use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wild animal or similar creature that is pursued, hunted, trapped, or caught.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine noun for the object of the chase, including the female wild ass pursued by a male.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A group of camels driven away together, including camels stolen or seized by mounted attackers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun use applied to camels carried off or driven away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A notched cane or small wooden tool used to smooth spindles, sticks, or arrows by repeatedly drawing them through it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized implement sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An oblong piece or long strip of cloth, silk, or rag; also a wetted rag used to wipe an oven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A material-object sense covering several cloth and rag applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A narrow strip of herbage or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a narrow elongated tract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The line or streak between the rump-bone and the withers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A game played by Arab desert children, also played by girls, involving touching parts of another player's body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized name for the game; some details of its terminology are reported as not firmly established.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small, swift kind of ship or boat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry is reported with some textual uncertainty about the form, but gives this as a lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who prolongs a recitation, especially Quran recitation, so as to drive listeners away by the length of the standing or reading.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative agent noun based on driving people away through excessive duration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wide, spacious, or ample, applied to a plain, place, roof, or region.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended adjectival use; regions may be described as spacious in which the mirage appears to flow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long, whole, or complete in duration, applied to a day, month, or year.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A temporal adjectival use describing an entire or extended period.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels that remain behind the others, as though driving the others onward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural expression for lagging camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short spear used for hunting or piercing wild animals, especially wild asses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An instrument noun associated with driving or pursuing game.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A means of driving away or removing something, especially a means of removing disease from the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of means or instrument in an extended medical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The beaten track or the main, middle part of a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun for the principal or central course of a road.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Apparently, a spear that is altogether straight, so that its whole length trembles rather than bends.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare poetic attribution, reported with a possibility of textual error or poetic license.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Following an even, continuous, or regular course; hence applied to a stream, running camel, horse's breathing, spear, coat of mail, speech, or other regularly ordered thing, and to a word, rule, or usage that conforms consistently to analogy or common practice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended adjectival sense of continuity and uniformity across physical objects, speech, and linguistic rules.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For sand, having one part drive away and follow another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of successive, shifting sand.

cautions: The Quranic nominal group طَارِد is presented under the singular active-participle citation form, not the inflected Quranic بِطَارِدِ.
Several Classical Arabic entries are rare or explicitly qualified as possible mistranscriptions; those qualifications are retained in their usage conditions rather than treated as Quranic evidence.
